title: Degree: base change and tensor products
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X$ a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $\dim X\le1$ [def-pc-dimension], and let $\mathcal{L},\mathcal{M}$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules [def-sc-invertible-module]. Write $\chi$ for the Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and $\deg=\chi(-)-\chi(\mathcal O)$ for the degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle].

1. (Base change) Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], $X_K:=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ with projection $p:X_K\to X$ [def-pc-base-change], and $\mathcal L_K:=p^*\mathcal L$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $X_K$ is proper over $K$, $\mathcal L_K$ is invertible, and
$\deg_{X_K}(\mathcal{L}_K)=\deg_X(\mathcal{L})$.
1. (Tensor with an effective divisor) Let $D\subset X$ be an effective Cartier divisor, i.e. the closed subscheme cut out by an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_D$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal] (on a curve: [def-sc-effective-cartier-divisor]), and $\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{O}_X(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Then $\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ and
$$
\deg(\mathcal{O}_X(D))=\dim_k\Gamma(D,\mathcal{O}_D),\qquad
\chi(X,\mathcal{L}\otimes\mathcal{M})=\deg(\mathcal{L})+\chi(X,\mathcal{M}),\qquad
\deg(\mathcal{L}\otimes\mathcal{M})=\deg(\mathcal{L})+\deg(\mathcal{M}).
$$
Moreover, let $P_1,\dots,P_m$ be closed points of $X$ with residue fields $\kappa(P_i)=k$ ($k$-rational points, [def-weil-residue-field]) such that each $P_i$ with its reduced induced structure, $[P_i]\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(P_i)$, is an effective Cartier divisor, let $n_1,\dots,n_m\in\mathbf Z$, and put $\mathcal O_X(\sum_in_i[P_i]):=\bigotimes_i\mathcal O_X([P_i])^{\otimes n_i}$ (a negative power meaning a power of the dual). Then $\deg(\mathcal{O}_X(\sum_in_i[P_i]))=\sum_in_i$.
1. (Additivity) For a short exact sequence of coherent modules
$0\to\mathcal{F}_1\to\mathcal{F}_2\to\mathcal{F}_3\to0$:
$\chi(X,\mathcal{F}_2)=\chi(X,\mathcal{F}_1)+\chi(X,\mathcal{F}_3)$
([lem-pc-euler-additive]).

proof.text: *(3).* This is exactly [lem-pc-euler-additive] (Stacks Tag 08AA: the long exact cohomology sequence of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces and rank–nullity).

*(1), the objects.* $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the base change of the proper morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence proper [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. By [def-pc-module-pullback], $p^*$ commutes with restriction to opens ($p^*(\mathcal G|_U)=(p^*\mathcal G)|_{p^{-1}U}$) and $p^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X_K}\otimes_{p^{-1}\mathcal O_X}p^{-1}\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X_K}$; so on an open $U$ with $\mathcal L|_U\cong\mathcal O_U$ one gets $\mathcal L_K|_{p^{-1}U}\cong\mathcal O_{p^{-1}U}$, and these $p^{-1}U$ cover $X_K$: $\mathcal L_K$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module]. As $X_K$ is of finite type over the field $K$ it is Noetherian, so the invertible modules $\mathcal L_K$, $\mathcal O_{X_K}$ are coherent and $\chi(X_K,\mathcal L_K)$, $\chi(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$, $\deg_{X_K}(\mathcal L_K)$ are defined.

*(1), the computation.* A field extension $K$ is a free, hence flat, $k$-module, so flat base change [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] (Stacks 02KH) applied to the quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal O_X$ (with $p^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X_K}$ from the previous step) gives, for every $i\ge0$, isomorphisms of $K$-vector spaces
$$H^i(X_K,\mathcal L_K)\cong H^i(X,\mathcal L)\otimes_kK,\qquad H^i(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})\cong H^i(X,\mathcal O_X)\otimes_kK .$$
By [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] the $k$-vector spaces $H^i(X,\mathcal L)$, $H^i(X,\mathcal O_X)$ are finite-dimensional and nonzero for only finitely many $i$; by [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change], $\dim_K(H^i(X,\mathcal F)\otimes_kK)=\dim_kH^i(X,\mathcal F)$ for $\mathcal F=\mathcal L,\mathcal O_X$. Hence the alternating sums of [def-pc-euler-characteristic] agree term by term: $\chi(X_K,\mathcal L_K)=\chi(X,\mathcal L)$ and $\chi(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ (Stacks 08AB), and by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]
$$\deg_{X_K}(\mathcal L_K)=\chi(X_K,\mathcal L_K)-\chi(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})=\chi(X,\mathcal L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=\deg_X(\mathcal L).$$

source.place: Tag 0B59, proof: 'By Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KH we have $H^i(X_{k'},\mathcal{E}_{k'})=H^i(X,\mathcal{E})\otimes_kk'$ and $H^i(X_{k'},\mathcal{O}_{X_{k'}})=H^i(X,\mathcal{O}_X)\otimes_kk'$. Hence ... the Euler characteristics are unchanged'; Tag 08AB, proof

proof.text: *(2), finiteness of $D$.* By [lem-pc-cartier-divisor-finite-over-field], $\dim D\le0$, $D$ is affine and finite over $k$, and $\delta:=\dim_k\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0AYY (varieties-lemma-degree-effective-Cartier-divisor), proof: 'Since $D$ is nowhere dense in $X$ ... $\dim(D)\leq0$. Hence $D$ is finite over $k$'

proof.text:
*(2), the exact sequence.* Let $i:D\to X$ be the closed immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] the map $i^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_D$ is surjective, and its kernel is the ideal sheaf $\mathcal I_D$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; so $0\to\mathcal I_D\to\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_D\to0$ is exact. The ideal $\mathcal I_D$ is invertible [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible], $\mathcal O_X(D)=\mathcal I_D^\vee$ is invertible [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-invertible], hence so is $\mathcal N:=\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_X(D)$ [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible]. Tensoring with an invertible module is exact: exactness of a sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules is checked on stalks, $(\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal N)_x=\mathcal G_x\otimes_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}\mathcal N_x$, and $\mathcal N_x\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. So
$$0\to\mathcal I_D\otimes\mathcal N\to\mathcal N\to i_*\mathcal O_D\otimes\mathcal N\to0$$
is exact. By associativity and commutativity of $\otimes$ and the isomorphism $\mathcal I_D\otimes\mathcal I_D^\vee\cong\mathcal O_X$ of [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] (applied to the invertible $\mathcal I_D$), $\mathcal I_D\otimes\mathcal N\cong\mathcal L\otimes(\mathcal I_D\otimes\mathcal I_D^\vee)\cong\mathcal L$. Hence an exact sequence
$$0\to\mathcal L\to\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_X(D)\to i_*\mathcal O_D\otimes\mathcal N\to0 .$$

source.place: Tag 0AYY, proof: 'By Divisors, Definition 01WX there is a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal{O}_X\to\mathcal{O}_X(D)\to i_*i^*\mathcal{O}_X(D)\to0$ ... Tensoring with $\mathcal{E}$ we obtain a short exact sequence'

proof.text:
*(2), the Euler characteristic of the quotient.* Put $\mathcal F:=i_*\mathcal O_D$. On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the Noetherian scheme $X$ (finite type over $k$) one has $\mathcal F|_U=\widetilde{A/I}$ with $I=\mathcal I_D(U)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], a finitely generated module over the Noetherian ring $A$, so $\mathcal F$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]; its stalk $\mathcal F_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathcal I_{D,x}$ is nonzero exactly for $x\in D$, so $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F=D$, of dimension $\le0$ by the finiteness step. By [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] (Stacks 0AYT (3)–(5)) applied to $\mathcal F$ and the invertible $\mathcal N$: $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal N$ is coherent and
$$\chi(X,i_*\mathcal O_D\otimes\mathcal N)=\chi(X,\mathcal F)=\dim_k\Gamma(X,i_*\mathcal O_D)=\dim_k\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)=\delta ,$$
the last equality being the definition of the pushforward, $\Gamma(X,i_*\mathcal O_D)=\Gamma(i^{-1}X,\mathcal O_D)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYY, proof: 'The equation of the lemma follows from ... Lemma 0AYT'; Tag 0AYT (varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite) (3)-(5)

proof.text:
*(2), the formulas.* The three terms of the exact sequence are coherent ($\mathcal L$, $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_X(D)$ are invertible on the Noetherian $X$; the third by the previous step), so additivity (3) [lem-pc-euler-additive] gives
$$\chi(X,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_X(D))=\chi(X,\mathcal L)+\delta\qquad(\ast)$$
for every invertible $\mathcal L$. For $\mathcal L=\mathcal O_X$ (with $\mathcal O_X\otimes\mathcal O_X(D)\cong\mathcal O_X(D)$) this is $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X(D))=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)+\delta$, i.e. $\deg\mathcal O_X(D)=\delta=\dim_k\Gamma(D,\mathcal O_D)$ by [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. With $\mathcal M=\mathcal O_X(D)$, $(\ast)$ and $\chi(X,\mathcal L)=\deg\mathcal L+\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ give $\chi(X,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)=\deg\mathcal L+\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)+\delta=\deg\mathcal L+\chi(X,\mathcal M)$, and subtracting $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$: $\deg(\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal M)=\deg\mathcal L+\delta=\deg\mathcal L+\deg\mathcal M$.

source.place: Tag 0AYY, statement 'deg(E(D)) = n deg(D) + deg(E)' with $n=1$ and its proof: 'The equation of the lemma follows from additivity of the Euler characteristic (Lemma 08AA)'

proof.text: *(2), rational points.* Let $P$ be a closed point with $\kappa(P)=k$ such that $[P]$ is an effective Cartier divisor. The reduced induced closed subscheme on the closed point $P$ is the one-point reduced scheme whose local ring is a field, namely $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(P)$ [def-weil-residue-field]; so $\Gamma([P],\mathcal O_{[P]})=\kappa(P)=k$ and, by the previous step, $\deg\mathcal O_X([P])=1$ and $\deg(\mathcal L'\otimes\mathcal O_X([P]))=\deg\mathcal L'+1$ for every invertible $\mathcal L'$. Applying this to $\mathcal L'':=\mathcal L'\otimes\mathcal O_X([P])^\vee$ (invertible by [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible]), for which $\mathcal L''\otimes\mathcal O_X([P])\cong\mathcal L'\otimes(\mathcal O_X([P])^\vee\otimes\mathcal O_X([P]))\cong\mathcal L'$ by [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible], gives $\deg(\mathcal L'\otimes\mathcal O_X([P])^\vee)=\deg\mathcal L'-1$ (the degree depends only on the isomorphism class, since $\chi$ does: isomorphic modules have isomorphic cohomology). Starting from $\deg\mathcal O_X=0$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] and tensoring one factor $\mathcal O_X([P_i])^{\pm1}$ at a time, induction on $\sum_i|n_i|$ gives $\deg\bigl(\bigotimes_i\mathcal O_X([P_i])^{\otimes n_i}\bigr)=\sum_in_i$.

source.place: Tag 0AYY (statement: $\deg(D)=\dim_k\Gamma(D,\mathcal{O}_D)$), applied to $D=[P]$; the induction follows the blueprint's last sentence ('$\deg(\mathcal{O}_X(D))=\sum_in_i\deg(\mathcal{O}_X([P_i]))=\sum_in_i$')
